**Region Midtjylland** and **Midtjylland** represent the organizational and geographical dimensions, respectively, of the same administrative area in [[danmark|Danmark]]. In the context of the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB), "Region Midtjylland" refers to the regional healthcare organization responsible for data submission, governance, and clinical operations, while "Midtjylland" designates the geographical and statistical region where specific hospitals are located and patient outcomes are measured. Together, they provide a comprehensive picture of acute surgical quality in the central part of the country.

### Organizational Role and Governance
As an organization, Region Midtjylland is one of the five Danish regions that report data to the AKDB. It actively engages with the database's governance, having submitted official comments on the 2023 annual report [^src3]. The region's organizational performance is frequently highlighted in national comparisons, often appearing at the extremes of quality indicators. For example, Region Midtjylland achieved the highest national performance for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] (administration of antibiotics within three hours of hospital arrival) at 44.6% [^src4]. Conversely, it also recorded the lowest 30-day mortality rate for [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] at 9.9% [^src2]. However, data quality remains an area of focus; the region reported the highest proportion of missing patient information for [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] at 15% [^src6], with 5% of all observations missing information primarily in this region [^src6].

### Geographical Profile and Hospital Network
Geographically, Midtjylland encompasses a network of major acute surgical departments. The region contains several key hospitals, including [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]], [[hospitalsenhed-midt|Hospitalsenhed Midt]], [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]], [[regionshospitalet-horsens|Regionshospitalet Horsens]], and [[regionshospitalet-randers|Regionshospitalet Randers]] [^src14]. When analyzing patient demographics across [[danmark|Danmark]], supplementary data shows that the [[asa-score|ASA]] scores and patient [[alder]] (age) for operated patients in Midtjylland do not differ significantly from those in [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] [^src9] [^src15].

### Chronological Performance Trends
The AKDB reports track the region's performance over distinct annual periods, revealing both improvements and ongoing challenges:

**01.09.2022 – 31.08.2023:**
During this period, Midtjylland achieved a 39.8% compliance rate for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] [^src11]. For the supplementary metric [[indikator-5x]], which measures the proportion of patients operated on within six hours for perforation, ischemia, or bleeding, the region reached 27.2% (66 out of 243 patients) [^src12]. Furthermore, the 30-day mortality rate for patients with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]] was recorded at 10.7% [^src14].

**01.09.2023 – 31.08.2024:**
In the subsequent year, the region's compliance for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] improved to 44.6% [^src16]. Other regional comparisons for this period showed varied results: the region reached 41.8% for [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] (compared to 25.9% in Region Sjælland) [^src17], 18.1% for [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] (compared to 4.3% in Region Hovedstaden) [^src5], and 46.4% for [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] (compared to 20.3% in Region Nordjylland) [^src7].

By mapping the administrative actions of Region Midtjylland to the statistical outcomes recorded in Midtjylland, the AKDB provides a transparent view of how regional healthcare policies translate into patient outcomes across central Denmark.
